solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Organic coal and Big Oil in conflict (10)

indicatorNotes.in conflict: letters at war with each other end up scrambled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters; 'and' just joins the two words

annotation.surface: Environmentalists pit organic farming against the fossil-fuel industry of coal and the oil majors.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets organic against coal and oil as rivals, but 'Organic' is simply the definition, and the fuels are raw letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Biological produce is organic, grown without synthetic chemicals.

entries.clue: Where takeaway choices may be ordained (2,6)

blocks.note: the dishes you pick from a takeaway menu are listed in your orders
a priest who has been ordained is in holy orders

annotation.surface: A whimsical picture of a takeaway menu being consecrated by a bishop.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is playful: the dishes you choose from a takeaway are in your orders. A priest who has been ordained is said to be in holy orders.
annotation.definitionFit: Takeaway choices sit in customers' orders, and a clergyman is 'in orders' once ordained.

entries.clue: Capable of concealing sign (3)

indicatorNotes.concealing: the phrase before it holds the answer inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

annotation.surface: Someone able to hide a signal or gesture.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the gap between the two words: capab(LE O)f.
annotation.definitionFit: Sign here means a sign of the zodiac, and the lion is one of the twelve.

entries.clue: Boasting about American genius (5)

indicatorNotes.about: one word goes around the other

blocks.note: gas = boastful talk
US = American

annotation.surface: A bragging American who claims to be a genius.
annotation.walkthrough: Carl Friedrich Gauss was a German mathematician often called the prince of mathematics, so the American is not the genius.
annotation.definitionFit: Gauss is one of history's great mathematical geniuses.

entries.clue: Cyprus harbours endless grievance, likely to fall apart (7)

indicatorNotes.harbours: Cyprus holds the other word inside, as a harbour holds a ship
indicatorNotes.endless: the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: CY is the international vehicle code for Cyprus
rumble = a complaint or grievance, minus its final E

annotation.surface: Cyprus nursing a long-standing grievance that threatens to split it, as the island has been split.
annotation.walkthrough: C(RUMBL)Y. The surface evokes the divided island, which makes 'fall apart' look political rather than a description of stale cake.
annotation.definitionFit: Something crumbly readily breaks into pieces.

entries.clue: Deploy mouse over cold stuff (4-5)

blocks.note: left over = remaining, so over = left
C = cold, as on a tap
to stuff an opponent is to beat them soundly, to lick them

annotation.surface: A cat setting a mouse loose over some chilly food.
annotation.walkthrough: The mouse is a computer's, not a rodent's. 'Stuff' means thrash, as in 'we got stuffed 5-0'.
annotation.definitionFit: You deploy a computer mouse by pressing its left button.

entries.clue: Possibly inappropriate part of speech has moved you (3-1)

indicatorNotes.has moved: the U is taken from its place and set elsewhere

blocks.note: NOUN with its U taken out
U sounds like 'you', in text-speak; here it moves to the end

annotation.surface: A pupil told that a word they used was improper grammar and it upset them.
annotation.walkthrough: NOUN becomes NONU when its U shifts to the back. Non-U, from Nancy Mitford's era, means not used by the upper class, so socially inappropriate.
annotation.definitionFit: Non-U usage is thought unsuitable among the upper classes, so possibly inappropriate.

entries.clue: Lionesses struggling with empty locality still (11)

indicatorNotes.struggling: the lionesses thrash about, their letters jumbled
indicatorNotes.empty: the word is emptied, keeping only its first and last letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
L(ocalit)Y

annotation.surface: Lionesses fighting over a deserted patch of land, yet somehow silent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as 'nevertheless' in the surface; it is the adverb 'silently'. The Lionesses are also England's women's football team.
annotation.definitionFit: To move noiselessly is to move still, without a sound.

entries.clue: Charles de Gaulle’s refusal to store more, mostly in hold (6)

indicatorNotes.to store: the refusal keeps the other word inside it
indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, dropping its last letter

blocks.note: non is French for no, as de Gaulle famously said to British entry into the Common Market
else = more, minus its last E

annotation.surface: De Gaulle refusing to let more goods be kept in a ship's hold.
annotation.walkthrough: N(ELS)ON. 'Hold' looks like a ship's cargo space; it is a wrestling hold, the nelson, applied from behind the opponent.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-favourite sense: the nelson is a wrestler's grip, arms under the opponent's and hands behind the neck.

entries.clue: Capital of America [?] to celebrate short Scottish singer (8)

indicatorNotes.of America: use the American spelling of the next word
indicatorNotes.short: a word that falls short of its full length is missing its end, so HONOR loses its R

blocks.note: to honor (American spelling) = to celebrate, cut short to HONO
Lulu is the Scottish pop singer of 'Shout'

annotation.surface: A capital city in America set up to honour a Scottish pop star.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of America' reads as part of the definition but tells you to spell honour the US way, HONOR, before cutting the R. Honolulu is the capital of Hawaii.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Hawaii's seat of government is one of fifty US state capitals.

entries.clue: A bit left in Sprite? (6)

indicatorNotes.in: one letter goes inside the word

blocks.note: a sprite is a fairy
L = left

annotation.surface: A little drop of fizzy lemonade still in the bottle.
annotation.walkthrough: FAIR(L)Y. The capital S makes Sprite the soft drink; it is a small fairy.
annotation.definitionFit: Fairly means somewhat, a bit, as in 'fairly tired'.

entries.clue: Converts plug by fitting sulphur (6)

blocks.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an ad
beside: the pieces sit next to each other
apt = fitting
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

annotation.surface: Someone altering an electrical plug to take a different fitting.
annotation.walkthrough: Plug and fitting both look electrical; plug means to advertise, and fitting means suitable.
annotation.definitionFit: Whoever adapts something converts it to a new use.

entries.clue: Pressure on firm getting into traditional drink determined in advance (11)

blocks.note: P = pressure, the physics symbol
re = on, concerning
mead, the old honey wine
firm = sure, certain

annotation.surface: Pressure on a company to join a heritage drinks market.
annotation.walkthrough: P + RE + MEA(SURE)D. 'Firm' pretends to be a business; it means certain.
annotation.definitionFit: Premeasured quantities are fixed, determined, before use.

entries.clue: Single part rejected by composer (8)

blocks.note: J.S. Bach
beside: the part goes next to the composer
a part in a play is a role

annotation.surface: A single instrumental part turned down by the composer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like a record or a solo line; it is the unmarried person.
annotation.definitionFit: Single is used as a noun: an unmarried man, the plain sense of the answer.

entries.clue: Shooting the wrong way in football match, perhaps getting sack (8,4)

blocks.note: a friendly is a match with nothing at stake; 'perhaps' shows it is one example
joins the two pieces
to sack is to fire

annotation.surface: A footballer shooting at his own goal in a friendly and being dropped for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shooting the wrong way' sounds like an own goal; it means soldiers firing on their own side.
annotation.definitionFit: Friendly fire is gunfire that hits your own forces, aimed the wrong way.

entries.clue: Defender of literature chewed cud with voters (4,5)

indicatorNotes.chewed: the letters are chewed over and mashed up

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters; 'with' just joins them

annotation.surface: A literary champion chewing the cud with the electorate, like a folksy candidate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Defender of literature' sounds like a campaigner or critic; it is the paper jacket that protects a book.
annotation.definitionFit: A dust cover shields a book from dirt and wear.

entries.clue: Welcoming South American playing old instrument (8)

blocks.note: SA = South America(n)
luting = playing the lute, an old stringed instrument

annotation.surface: A South American musician greeting guests on an antique instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Luting' is a verb made from the lute: the setter needs a word meaning 'playing the lute'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a salute is a gesture of greeting, so both words describe receiving someone warmly.

entries.clue: A patient asks about Bangladesh before sovereignty (4,8)

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A hospital patient enquiring about Bangladesh's history before independence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning'; it scrambles the letters before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Bangladesh was East Pakistan until it won independence in 1971.

entries.clue: Swan trap snaring head of unusual bird (7)

indicatorNotes.snaring: the trap catches the letter inside it

blocks.note: a pen is a female swan
a gin is a snare or trap
first letter of unusual

annotation.surface: A trap set for swans catching a strange bird by mistake.
annotation.walkthrough: PEN + G(U)IN. 'Gin' as a trap is short for engine; gin-traps are old snares.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the flightless Antarctic swimmer is one kind of bird.

entries.clue: Produce Times comic from 1930s (6)

blocks.note: to form is to produce or create
times = by, as in three by four

annotation.surface: The Times newspaper bringing out a comic strip from the 1930s.
annotation.walkthrough: George Formby was a British comic singer and film star, hugely popular in the 1930s with his ukulele. 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign.
annotation.definitionFit: George Formby was a leading comedian of 1930s British film.

entries.clue: French chapter replacing intro to holy book, accepting that’s how it was written? (8)

indicatorNotes.replacing: one letter takes the place of another
indicatorNotes.accepting: the word takes another inside it

blocks.note: C = chapter
the first letter of the holy book, K, is the one that goes
the Koran, Islam's scripture
sic, Latin 'thus', is put after a quoted error to say it was written that way

annotation.surface: A French chapter heading swapped in for the opening of a scripture, with a note that the text is quoted as found.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'French' as an adjective for the chapter; it is the definition, and the question mark admits that an islander from Corsica is only French in a political sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Corsica is part of France, so a Corsican is, in a sense, French.

entries.clue: What could give old man wage reduction (3,3)

blocks.note: read as an instruction, PAY with Y cut gives PA, the old man

annotation.surface: Wondering what an elderly man could be given, then answering with a drop in wages.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer read as an instruction, cut the Y from PAY, leaves PA, a word for father, the old man.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a wage reduction, while the whole phrase read as an instruction, cut Y from PAY, yields the old man.

entries.clue: Steal fruit, expending energy for nothing (5)

indicatorNotes.for: in exchange for: the O takes its place

blocks.note: a peach is a fruit
E = energy, the letter that goes
O = nothing, zero, the letter that comes in

annotation.surface: Stealing fruit, and doing it for nothing, without spending effort.
annotation.walkthrough: PEACH swaps its E for an O.
annotation.definitionFit: To poach is to steal, especially game or staff.

entries.clue: Better to skip last performance without rehearsal (6)

indicatorNotes.to skip last: to skip something is to leave it out, so the word leaves out its last letter

blocks.note: improve = better, losing its last letter E

annotation.surface: Advice that you'd do better to skip the final performance if you haven't rehearsed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb here, to improve, not a comparative.
annotation.definitionFit: Short for improvisation: theatre or comedy made up on the spot, with nothing rehearsed.

entries.clue: Confident United supporter backing attack (8)

indicatorNotes.backing: going backwards, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: U = United, as in football team names
a supporter is a fan
a raid is an attack

annotation.surface: A cocky Manchester United fan cheering on the team's attack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like 'supporting', which suits a supporter; here it turns FAN round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having no fear means facing things with confidence.

entries.clue: P for Pythagoras? (3)

blocks.note: the surface reading: the English letter P, as in an alphabet primer
the setter's reading: Pythagoras was Greek, so ask what a Greek would call the letter shaped like P

annotation.surface: A classroom label: P is for Pythagoras.
annotation.walkthrough: 'P for Pythagoras' looks like an alphabet primer; Pythagoras was Greek, and in the Greek alphabet the letter written P is rho.
annotation.definitionFit: Rho is the Greek letter whose capital looks like a Latin P.

entries.clue: Observed fish under discussion (4)

indicatorNotes.under discussion: being talked about, so spoken out loud

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: A fish being watched while people talk about it.
annotation.walkthrough: The ide, a carp-like fish, is a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to observe something is to watch it, to run your eyes over it.

entries.clue: Doubly hard to follow small creature in practice (3-7)

indicatorNotes.Doubly: use 'hard' twice, in two different forms
indicatorNotes.to follow: what follows comes after, so the hard pieces go after the creature

blocks.note: the runt is the smallest of a litter
H = hard, as on pencils
rough = hard, harsh

annotation.surface: Something doubly hard to follow when it's a tiny animal you are tracking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doubly hard to follow' reads as 'very difficult to understand'; instead it asks for two different words for hard, placed after the creature.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatre sense: running through a show from start to finish is how a cast practises it.
